Review: The one star is for the nursing staff, aides and ancillary personnel who attended my husband during his stay for rehabilitation. However, the physician and nurse practitioner assigned to the facility were terrible, showing little or no interest in my husband during his almost three week stay. Mainly because they only saw him once (the doctor) and twice (the NP), despite my requests to meet with them. They never saw or acknowledged and thus ignored, my husbabd’s rapid decline.  The doctor never saw him after the initial “admitting assessment”—actually telling me, as I cornered him in the hallway,  that he “didn't want to get into the NPs lane.”  It made me question his driving ability. The facility is shabby and depressing.  It was recently purchased from another company (whose reputation was awful)and instead of closing it down and at least painting the rooms, they obviously just changed the locks. The rooms were “furnished” with what  looked as if they had just backed a truck up to a Goodwill store and took whatever they had. The walls had gouges in them where the previous beds and equipment had been ripped out.  The beds were old.  There were days the toilet backed up and brackish water would just sit.  The food was as unappealing as I’ve ever seen.  There were times when the entree was unrecognizable.  The “menu” was laughable since many times the stated food was “unavailable”.  One night they forgot to bring his dinner. One of the staff warned me to “get him out of here as soon as you can.” By that time it was too late.  To my eternal regret, my husband died there. Extrememly disappointed! My husband was admitted through the VA for respite care while I (wife and caregiver) took a trip to see my family.

I supplied Willowbrook with plenty of snacks so he would have food to eat if he didn’t like the meal that was offered. Also, left instructions for how meds were to be administered. I left detailed notes to help staff know what he likes and dislikes and how they can help make him happy.

I called everyday to check on him. I could tell he was unhappy and he wanted to go home. That broke my heart and I would hang up just worrying about how he was being treated.

A couple weeks in to the stay I got a call he fell out of bed. He has never fallen out of bed. I was informed of this and that he was not injured. I later found out he fell a second time and I never was informed of this. I was never notified that he indeed did sustain an injury.

He was to come home on the 5th. What I saw when he arrived was so upsetting. I couldn’t believe he came home with NONE of his belongings. Staff did not check to make sure he left with his clothes, personal belongings and extra food. He came home inappropriately dressed and he was freezing! He obviously had not been looked over to make sure he was adequately dressed. He was favoring his arm and I looked at it and his hand was curled up so tight and his arm was so badly bruised. Why was I not notified? When did this happen? What happened? His hand was numb and it hurt bad. I have instructions to take Tylenol around the clock so he would not be in any pain. I was told her didn’t ask for anything and it was prescribed as PRN. He doesn’t know enough to ask for it due to his declining disease. Was any of my instructions followed through? He was starving and so thirsty when he got home.

If they had not failed to notify us, we could’ve made the proper decision to get him the hell away from this place.

Then, this past week, they found him unconscious. AGAIN, they failed to notify us. We did not know that he had been transferred to the hospital until the surgeon reached out to his son, who is power of attorney, to ask if they could perform a procedure. Once we heard that he had been transferred to the hospital, 24 hours later, we then find out he was without oxygen for so long that he is now suffering from brain damage. Why are nursing staff not rounding on their patients? And short staffed is not the answer! the only answer is they do not care, and this place needs to be SHUT DOWN!

Thanks to the carelessness and pure disrespect of this facility, we are now stuck watching our dad, brother, and grandpa suffer and fight for his life. Just last week he was fine, and now he is receiving end of life care. He went from a healthy; responsive man to a man who is unable to eat, drink, or communicate.

If you value your loved ones, do some research and save them from this hell hole. Nobody deserves this treatment. Especially not someone who is dependent on caregivers.

I hope the kind of care they have exhibited so far, will continue for mom.

Review: The Doctors, PA, Nurses, Threapy, CNAs, and housekeeping were simply amazing. I have zero complaints about them. My one huge complaint is the food. While I was there I had to spend hundreds on doordash because the food that's served is absolutely disgusting and if it was something edible you got a very small portion. The kitchen needs some serious help. They tried passing nasty black eye peas off as baked beans, I asked multiple times more than 15 times time for them to send me grits instead of oatmeal with my breakfast and they wouldn't. Also the timing of the meals was never the same. It could vary as much as 3 hours post the posted times meals where meant to be served.

Yall lemme tell you… I came to visit my friend fully prepared to feel guilty and sad, but this place ruined that plan by actually being wonderful. The staff are ridiculously kind and somehow manage to juggle ten things at once while still remembering everyone’s name (and snack preferences). The nurses deserve an award for their patience — they’ve got the energy of a coffee shop on Monday morning and the compassion of a Hallmark movie. The building is clean, smells nice (which, let’s be honest, is rare in healthcare), and the residents actually “laugh” here. Like, real laughter — not the polite kind you do at family dinners. Every time I visit, I end up staying longer than I planned because it just feels good to be here. If every nursing facility ran like this one, people might actually look forward to aging. Five stars for making care look effortless — and for proving that kindness and sarcasm can happily coexist. The young lady at the front I believe she’s the social worker Shalimar, unbelievably kind with the warmest heart. AND the DOR there is literally the greatest to ever do it. enough said🙌🏽

Review:
If I could give this facility less than 1 star, I would. This place is horrible!! Most of the staff that I dealt with there had a bad attitude and seemed lazy and unconcerned with patients' care or comfort. Most staff members, except for just a couple, are very rude, impatient, and come across like they hate their jobs. The administrator doesn't LISTEN, & likes to cut you off when you're voicing a concern, trying to minimize problems. There's a huge calendar on the wall with activities posted on it, and at a glance it looks like there are plenty of things for residents to fill their days doing, and from what I could tell during the time that my loved one was there, even though its just the same 2 or 3 things over and over... bingo & ice cream socials are about the only positive points here. The dietary staff is very unfriendly and extremely rude, except for 1 cook, Ms. Dee. She was the only one of them who didn't seem angry when my uncle had a special request, and I did witness her smiling and speaking to the residents in the dining room before serving their meal on more than 1 occassion. I have personally heard some be EXTREMELY rude to residents and even ignore them when they ask for something. It is quite obvious that the staff does not want to be there.
On one particular visit, I chose to have lunch in the dining room with my loved one (He was in bed as always when I arrived & I had to get someone to help get him up), and it was impossible to relax & enjoy the meal due to all of the yelling and cursing & carrying on coming from the kitchen. There is zero level of professionalism back there. Patients are supposed to feel as if they're at home, but Pineview doesn't even come close to hitting the mark. Dining there is probably better compared to a jail or a bad, underfunded school cafeteria.
During another visit to see a loved one, I personally witnessed a woman sitting in a wheelchair (directly in front of the nurse's station window) gagging and vomiting, soiling her pants and shirt. 4 employees were sitting in the nurse's station while this took place that saw her, but NONE of them got up to assist the woman! After vomiting, the woman proceeded to take her soiled shirt off in the hallway. When I left the facility, about 1 1/2 hours later, this woman was still sitting in front of the nurse's station, in the same soiled pants and a blanket covering the top part of her body.
Another time, I arrived to find my loved one with feces under his fingernails and lying in a soiled bed. He didn't know how long he'd been there, but it was over 20 minutes from the time I asked for help cleaning him up to the time someone actually came to help. Every single time I popped in to visit, I found my uncle in bed. No matter what time of day I went by, he was in bed. My loved one has been moved since this incident.
I STRONGLY urge you to check on your family if they are having to live there!!
I could write pages of examples like the few I've mentioned. We found another facility thankfully and moved my uncle and to no real surprise, his UTI is gone ( he KEPT one almost the whole time he was there!!!), he has no bedsores, and his depression has GREATLY improved!! I hope this review will be a wake-up call to people who have family members living at Pineview and will make those considering it think twice before using it. It costs a lot of money to reside at this facility, and by NO means does a patient get their money's worth!!

A staff member responded with remarkable urgency and clinical acumen, swiftly assessing the situation and escalating it to the nursing team. Their meticulous attention to cleanliness, coupled with consistent courtesy, respect for privacy, and cheerful demeanor, contributed significantly to my well-being and comfort. Their unwavering positivity, irrespective of daily demands, is truly commendable.

I wholeheartedly recommend the Newport News Nursing Rehab Center to any individual seeking rehabilitation services, whether for short-term recovery or long-term care. Their holistic approach, which seamlessly integrates unparalleled medical and therapeutic expertise with genuine compassion, creates an environment supremely conducive to healing and comprehensive recovery. My deepest appreciation goes to each and every member of the team whose professionalism, empathy, and consistent encouragement were instrumental in my journey to recovery.

Review:
First, let me say that I’m not giving a 5-star review because everything was perfect at Emerald Ridge or because every staff member was exemplary (that is an impossible standard for any facility).

I am giving a 5-star review because in the three years my brother was resident there with multiple serious health conditions, I spent a lot of time at the facility and interacting with staff and my experience was that the vast majority of staff at Emerald Ridge were highly-competent, very caring and compassionate and very diligent about doing their very best with the resources given.

Could more attention be given to certain areas -- food yes, laundary yes - but that is true everywhere.

What counts is that I never lacked confidence in his care, and indeed, almost everyone I dealt with, from nurses, to CNAs, to PT, to the receptionist, to records, to billing, to the activities director to the cleaning staff, to the transport person, were always attentive and responsive to my brother’s needs and by extension, my own. Indeed, I came to feel like part of the Emerald Ridge  family.

I also appreciated their transparency in calling me even when an innocuous mistake was made (which again, is not possible to avoid anywhere) and their encouragement of staff to speak up, as I found that evidence of extraordinary integrity.

Throughout his time there, and particularly up to my brother’s death. I witnessed extraordinary acts of kindness, for which I am truly thankful

Review:
Following surgery at Riverside Regional Center, I was subsequently admitted to the Jamestown Health and Rehabilitation facility (Consulate Health Care of Williamsburg).
Upon entering the building on a stretcher, I felt disgust. I was shocked that Riverside had sent me to such a facility.
I immediately contacted my children. My son arrived promptly and expressed his disgust. He informed me that he would arrange for my release. However, he was informed that coordinating a move with other centers at 7:00 pm was impossible. The only options available were to stay overnight or take me home, but this was not feasible given my fractured femur.
I refrained from interacting with any of the staff members, as I felt a sense of resentment towards them due to the poor conditions of my surroundings.
The following day, my son spoke with the insurance company, and they offered limited accommodations therefore despite
the challenging circumstances, I remained at the facility. A friend and my children provided me with food, drinks, and other necessities.
As the days progressed, I began to appreciate the kindness of the employees. Most of them have been working here for several years. I discovered a flower garden and a room dedicated to various daily activities. However, one of my medications was unfortunately out of stock for a couple of days. Despite this setback, the staff was extremely generous with pain medication and provided me with all the medications I take at home.
The rehabilitation trainers were exceptional.The case worker’s efforts were remarkable in persuading the insurance company to provide me with the necessary equipment. A team of professionals collaborated to ensure that all the required arrangements were made.
However, I must acknowledge that I had some reservations about the food. I never ate their food.
Despite these minor concerns, I remained at the facility for five days. Initially, my experience was quite unpleasant, but it transformed into a positive one. I am deeply appreciative of each and every staff member for their kindness and support. Life is unpredictable, and I am fortunate to have encountered such a compassionate and caring environment.

Review:
I wanted to leave a review for Cardinal Healthcare and Rehabilitation Center for two reasons: (1) When I was looking for a qualified center to send my mom to, there was not always a lot of reviews to go by, so I want to help others, and (2) to thank the wonderful staff at Cardinal for the care, support, and compassion that they provided to my mom and myself.

I honestly was unsure what the level of care was going to be when my mom was getting discharged from the hospital to a rehabilitation center, and I hand selected Cardinal from a list of 10 centers that I was provided with by the hospital, and honestly the level of care FAR surpassed the “care” that she was receiving at the hospital.

I had daily interactions with the staff; from the administrators who came around all the time to check on residents, to the physical therapy team who are wonderful, to the delightful housekeeping team that is always around making sure all of the rooms and facility are spotless. The nursing staff that I interacted with were wonderful, and really cared about the level of care and comfort of the residents ( and they took care of me too!).
They check on the residents often, make sure that they are moving and not laying in one spot all day, help with anything that they can, and as I said before, were very supportive overall. I also can not forget to mention Ms. Barbara who is amazing and is a very special lady, who has so much empathy and compassion and she helped me get thru some hard days and would come and check on my mom as well.
There are some real “shining stars” working at this facility,  and as strange as it might sound, I will miss some of the interactions I had with the staff, and I am grateful to them for taking care of my mom and for putting up with me!
